pillar_reactions.evidence: He volunteered his own case for it and tied it directly to his goals: "I really wanted something that was dealing with... I want something that has more longevity and that covers more of what I do. In pickleball, you don't do this... you move all over the plate. And in volleyball, it's the same way." He also stated the outcome he wants in the programme's own terms — "I don't need to be super big and have huge muscles, but I do want to be lean, and I want my muscles to function as they're supposed to" — and endorsed the portability: "I was just on a cruise, and they did have kettlebells, I'm like, I can just do it from here."

Clear agreement with no resistance and no questions on mechanics: "Yeah, I'm on board with all that." He engaged with the sustainability framing rather than the rules — "It's not a prison sentence" — and corrected himself downward honestly on his own compliance: "Maybe I'm a 70-30 right now." The perfectionism reframe landed: "If I don't do it perfect, then I can't keep doing it."

The rep pre-empted the obvious doubt — "I guess there's a part of you sitting right now and wondering, is this just gonna be kind of the same?" — and the prospect confirmed it was live: "I mean, sure, it's in the back of my mind." He then tested it from his own professional standpoint ("for a living, I do exactly what you're doing right now") and probed the credibility of remote coaching generally: "how can you coach me if you're not going through what I'm going through?" He accepted the differentiators once given — Trevor coaching personally, video form feedback, weekly check-ins, direct cell number — responding "That's great", and immediately started planning around his travel week.

anchors.raw: It's definitely more expensive than my last group.
anchors.note: The direct price comparison, stated moments after the $6,000 reveal and never engaged with. The unusual feature is that the prospect had already discredited the cheaper option himself — cookie-cutter programming, weekly calls that were "kind of a joke", poor video feedback — so this anchor was more answerable than most. The rep never asked what it cost and never contrasted it.

anchors.raw: we're in the middle of a home remodel. It's costing $600,000. And that pretty much drains us of all of our liquid money.
anchors.note: Not a value objection — a liquidity one, and the same shape as several other deals in this corpus. He separately said "I make a decent living and so I can find a way to make that happen", so capacity exists and timing does not. This is the case a standard, non-premium instalment plan is for.

anchors.raw: that's why I hire a coach. I have a coach that works with me personally and my business. And it's been wonderful... I've hired coaches to help me do that. And it's always brought results.
anchors.note: He buys coaching routinely, judges it on outcomes, and does not regret any of it — "some coaches have been terrible... but I don't regret any one of them, because I've learned something every time." The strongest supportive anchor available on this call and it went entirely unused when price resistance arrived.

anchors.raw: Okay, so $1,000 a month. ... Isn't it a six-month program? ... I'm a financial advisor, so...
anchors.note: He did the monthly maths himself and unprompted, which normally signals a buyer working out how to say yes. The rep pushed back on the framing — "it's a transformation program, it's not just that you're training with a PT" — and argued against a reframe that was working in his favour. Worth noting that a financial advisor is likely to think in monthly terms regardless of how the offer is positioned.

unmet_demand.want: A way to buy that does not require paying $6,000 upfront to someone he has only met online
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No approved instalment structure was available to offer on the spot; the rep could only say "if there's a will, there's a way" and book another call to work it out. The guarantee that would ordinarily derisk this is a training-continuation promise, not money back, and the client agreement carries a no-refunds clause.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that loaded kettlebell training is safe given ruptured cervical discs, persistent hand nerve damage, a torn meniscus and an elbow that will not extend
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no clinical screen or clearance step in the process. The rep's answer was to defer the injuries to the onboarding call with Trevor — "So he will learn everything about you. Your injuries, your knee, elbow" — which routes a clinical question to a coach. The performance guarantee is itself framed as adding eight kilos to a baseline kettlebell, a load-progression promise with no medical qualification.

unmet_demand.want: Preparation specific to a 50-hour continuous endurance event
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep positioned the race explicitly as a milestone rather than the product — "the goal isn't just to get you to the Baha 1000 start line in November. That's, I would say, the first milestone" — which is honest but leaves the prospect's actual purchase trigger only partly served. Sleep deprivation and hand and grip endurance, the two things that ended his 2023 attempt, were not addressed on either leg of the conversation.
